subject: URGENT: Production latency incident - hosted to dedicated decision
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@acmeanalytics.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-07-12T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call: deployment mode recommendation for Acme Analytics

Hi Alex -

Thanks for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment: 

- Need: low-latency real-time inference for customer-facing product (90th pct latency target < 150ms for 2k qps peak).
- Current usage: spikes to ~1.5k qps for short bursts; avg ~300 qps.
- Data controls: no PHI, but sensitive customer PII; must meet SOC2 controls and enterprise auditability.
- Options we discussed: Hosted API (fastest go-live), Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pools for predictable throughput), Private (VPC/on-prem for strict network controls).

Initial recommendation: given the latency and burst profile, Dedicated capacity is the likeliest fit to guarantee throughput and predictable SLOs. Hosted could work short term but you may hit throttling during bursts. Private VPC is possible but will add multi-week lead time.

Next steps:
1) Can you confirm whether Acme has an immediate production incident risk window (e.g., upcoming campaign/launch) that would force an accelerated timeline?
2) I’ll loop in Rishi and Connor to draft a capacity estimate + timeline.
3) If you want, we can schedule a 30-min emergency sizing call - I’m available today 2-4pm PT.

Attachments: capacity-estimate.xlsx (preliminary template)

--
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com | +1 415-555-0186
From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@acmeanalytics.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-07-12T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: deployment mode recommendation for Acme Analytics

Marissa -

Appreciate the summary. Short answer: yes, we have an incident this morning. Our hosted integration started returning 503s during a marketing push; latency spiked and some customers are seeing errors. Engineering traced it to request queuing on the hosted tier when bursts exceed our current quota.

We need a plan within the next 48 hours. If Redwood can provide Dedicated capacity quickly (or a fast move to Private VPC with strict network controls), we’ll prioritize that. Procurement will need an SOW/price, but we can fast-track.

Please treat this as urgent - our product lead is escalating. I’m available for a call in 30 mins.

Thanks,
Alex Turner
Head of Product, Acme Analytics
alex.turner@acmeanalytics.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Alex Turner <alex.turner@acmeanalytics.com>
Date: 2026-07-12T10:25:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: URGENT: Production latency incident - hosted to dedicated decision

Folks - looping you in. Acme (external) just hit a production incident with hosted throttling during a marketing burst. They need options within 48 hours: 1) Dedicated capacity ASAP or 2) Private VPC (longer). Can you please: 

- Rishi: give a low-latency dedicated config we can commit to for 2k qps bursts (single-region preferred). Include estimated lead time, cost delta vs hosted, and any immediate gating items (e.g., contract/PO/infra access).
- Connor: confirm ops timeline to stand up a dedicated pool and any quick mitigations we can apply on hosted (burst quotas, temporary quota increase, emergency caching).

Attaching the capacity template I sent the customer. I’d like to turn this into a proposal and SOW to send procurement. 

Alex - we’re on it; will circle back with a recommended config in ~2-3 hours. If you can share expected peak qps by minute (or a link to monitoring), that’ll help.

--
Marissa
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Alex Turner <alex.turner@acmeanalytics.com>
Date: 2026-07-12T12:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: URGENT: Production latency incident - hosted to dedicated decision

Marissa / Connor / Alex -

Quick sizing and options based on the numbers so far:

1) Emergency Dedicated (recommended for 48-hour SLA-to-safety):
- Config: 4 x A100-equivalent GPUs in a dedicated pool with 4 inference workers, pre-warmed KV cache, optimized batching for short sequences.
- Expected steady throughput: ~1k qps; burst capacity up to ~2.5k qps with autoscale buffer.
- Timeline to stand up (fast path): ~24-36 hours if contract + PO approved and we get network ACLs for telemetry.
- Estimated monthly cost (ballpark): $65k- $80k (we’ll refine).

2) Short-term Hosted mitigations (if they need immediate relief, <24h):
- Temporary quota increase for the hosted route to buy time (requires approvals).
- Apply targeted rate limiting on cheaper non-customer-facing endpoints and enable prefix caching for repeated prompts.

3) Private VPC/on-prem:
- Feasible but longer: 3-6 weeks for network setup, VPC peering, and security approvals. Good for long-term compliance but not immediate.

Attachments: dedicated-config.pdf (prelim architecture and SLO table).

What I need from Acme to finalize: confirmed peak minute qps, whether they can accept single-region or need multi-region active-active, and an internal PO timeline.

I’ll draft an SOW and a short-term addendum for emergency capacity.

--
Rishi Malhotra
Sr. Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@acmeanalytics.com>, Procurement <procurement@acmeanalytics.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-07-14T17:42:00-07:00
Subject: URGENT: next steps - Dedicated capacity proposal & emergency call

Alex / Procurement team -

Thanks for the quick sync earlier. Per Rishi’s recommendation, we think the fastest, lowest-risk path to restore your SLA is Emergency Dedicated capacity (4x A100-equivalent pool). Summary of immediate next steps: 

1) Redwood will provision the dedicated pool on a fast-path within 24-36 hours once we have an approved PO and signed SOW addendum.
2) Rishi’s team will do the production handoff and pre-warm key caches before cutover.
3) We’ll keep the Hosted route as failover for non-critical traffic during the transition.

Action items: 
- Procurement: please review the attached SOW draft (acme-sow-draft.pdf) and send PO to finance@redwoodinference.com. We can accept an emailed PO and will follow up with DocuSign for the final SOW if you prefer (DocuSign: https://www.docusign.net/00A12345-ec5a-attach).
- Alex: please confirm peak minute qps and whether single-region is acceptable.
- Internal: Rishi / Connor please confirm final provision ETA once PO is in.

I’ll keep this thread updated. Thanks everyone for the quick turnaround - we’ll treat this as a priority.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com | +1 415-555-0186
